## The idea

Explain the concept, when it helps, and one important distinction. Write for public readers without referring to an authoring conversation or private request. Use a concrete example. Link substantive current claims to primary sources and identify the source date.

## Try it

State prerequisites and access needs. Give inputs and steps. Provide a starter prompt if useful. Label the task as proposed until you have recorded an actual run. Specify a budget or stopping condition where needed.

## Check your work

Supply an expected answer or rubric. Name essential failures, edge cases, and what the exercise does not establish.

## Teach it

Suggest a short demonstration, one learner exercise, and a teach-back question.

## Keep exploring

Link related lessons, a source record, and primary references. Complete the research and experiment record before publication.
